name: Kalshi Bot — System Map
description: High-level architecture and flow of the Kalshi trading system: data sources, the Railway worker pipeline (scan → candidate → risk → paper/live → twin), Postgres, Experiment OS governance, the evo agent fleet, and the operator/agent control plane.

elements.name: External venues & data sources

properties.purpose: Everything the system mirrors or calls but does not own.

intent: All of these are someone else's truth; the system stores snapshots so research is reproducible.

elements.name: Railway — main worker (BOT_MODE=live)

properties.purpose: The scan/trade cycle, all operator books, Experiment OS boot hooks and gate evaluation. The ONLY writer to production data.

intent: One process owns the whole cycle so that writes, risk and enforcement cannot be bypassed.

elements.name: Railway — evo worker (BOT_MODE=evo)

properties.purpose: The evolutionary LLM agent fleet, running on the same Postgres as the main worker.

intent: Second worker so agent cognition can never stall the trading cycle.

elements.name: Postgres (Railway) — single writer

properties.purpose: All durable state. Every non-worker path into it is read-only by construction.

intent: If the database is unavailable the worker exits — nothing trade-like proceeds.

elements.name: Experiment OS (in-worker, canonical for experiments)

properties.purpose: Lifecycle, versions, epochs, deployments, gates, evaluator, enforcement, platform impact, issues.

intent: Experiment truth lives here, not in docs or chat — docs go stale within a day.

elements.name: Operator & agent control plane

properties.purpose: How a human and an agent session observe and change the system from outside the runtime.

intent: The agent sandbox cannot reach Railway or Postgres, so every path in this zone is narrow and audited.

elements.name: Kalshi exchange (REST)

properties.interface: /trade-api/v2 — markets, order books, trades, orders, fills, settlements

intent: The venue. Order books are resting bids only, so the YES ask is derived as 100 − best NO bid.

elements.name: Weather providers

properties.interface: point forecasts, station observations, HRRR, multi-model ensembles

intent: Temperature buckets are priced off a distribution, so ensembles matter more than the point forecast.

elements.name: Polymarket (read-only)

properties.interface: Gamma / data API — same-day temperature and game markets

intent: Cross-venue reference price only; the system never trades Polymarket.

elements.name: Crypto spot feed
intent: Feeds the trailing spot-vol model that separates dead tails from live ones on hourly crypto ladders.

elements.name: LLM APIs
intent: Cognition for the evo fleet only — no LLM sits in the trading decision path.

elements.name: Fail-closed config

properties.responsibility: Load and validate settings, book/variant specs and risk caps before anything runs

intent: Bad config means the worker does nothing trade-like, rather than proceeding on defaults.

elements.name: Kalshi client + RSA-PSS auth

properties.responsibility: Sign and issue every exchange request; retry and fail closed on auth failure

intent: Single choke point for exchange credentials and for the signing scheme.

elements.name: Scanner

properties.responsibility: Fetch markets and order books, compute liquidity metrics, score deterministically, persist snapshots

intent: Deterministic scoring so a cycle can be replayed and audited.

elements.name: Per-book universe filter

properties.filters: only= / skip= (raw tickers), mtype= / mode= / xmtype= (taxonomy)

intent: A series with no taxonomy entry is admitted by NO allowlist filter — classification debt shows up as exclusion, never as a silent default.

elements.name: Strategy books

properties.responsibility: One package per book family: mmsell, theta, weather, freeze, pin15, tfav, wcprop, xgame

intent: Books run as parallel tags against the same tape so their P&L can be compared head-to-head.
A book is a question, not a product: proving one is −EV is a win.

elements.name: Candidate

properties.dataType: market × book × cycle, with the entry rule's edge attached

intent: The one object every execution path shares: paper, live and twin all consume the same candidate.

elements.name: Risk manager (fail-closed)

properties.responsibility: Gate every order intent: kill switch, mode, balance, spread/liquidity, closes-soon, per-market and total exposure, daily loss

intent: Refuses on any doubt. In paper mode the live-only gates are skipped, but every market and exposure gate still applies.

elements.name: Load-bearing safety machinery
intent: Kill switch, exposure caps, the fail-closed risk manager and the arming ritual are never weakened to make a task easier.
Anything that expands real-money exposure requires explicit operator confirmation.

elements.name: Paper engine

properties.responsibility: Simulate entries at the real quote, model Kalshi fees, manage exits, settle to 0/100

intent: Measurement harness, not a toy: edge is measured against the price actually paid, so the spread is netted out.
Its one structural lie is that a resting maker order always fills.

elements.name: Live executor

properties.responsibility: Place and manage real orders: maker pricing, dollar-cap sizing, queue-position modelling, exit rules

intent: Requires BOT_MODE=live, KILL_SWITCH=false and a tag on the live allowlist — three independent conditions.

elements.name: Paper twin harness

properties.responsibility: Run a fresh paper book beside each live tag with the live parameters; tape every per-candidate decision

intent: Controls sample, regime, sizing and concurrency so the only remaining difference is the fill assumption.
Separates an execution gap (live can't capture the trades) from an accounting gap (paper is wrong about trades we did get).

elements.name: PERP-V1 instrument tape

properties.responsibility: Read-only perpetual-futures tape; writes its own tables, carries no strategy tag, places nothing

intent: An instrument, not a book — runs in the every-mode cycle hook so coverage does not depend on BOT_MODE.

elements.name: Evidence funnel (obs)

properties.responsibility: Every series-addressed book emits a bounded funnel line naming the stage where its count first hit zero

intent: So 'this book saw no markets' can be told apart from 'this book was never asked' without reading raw logs.

elements.name: Evolutionary agent fleet

properties.responsibility: LLM agents that read the repo and live book performance, then propose and run their own books under a budget

intent: Agents are subject to the same registration and enforcement as operator books — no side door to trading.

elements.name: Evo historical search

properties.responsibility: search_strategy_space: replay a strategy plus a bounded neighbourhood of variants and return evidence

intent: A capability, not an experiment: own namespace, no lifecycle of its own, replay only and no live path.

elements.name: Evo capability tickets
intent: The fleet asks for capabilities it lacks instead of inventing unsafe workarounds; a human triages the queue.

elements.name: Market record

properties.data: markets, market_snapshots, orderbook_snapshots, signals, per-book candidate ticks

intent: The tape the whole research program is graded against.

elements.name: Trading record

properties.data: paper_trades, paper_positions, live_orders, fills, positions, account_snapshots, twin + parity tables

intent: Paper and live are stored side by side so the twin comparison is a query, not a reconstruction.

elements.name: Research inputs

properties.data: weather forecasts/observations/ensembles/buckets, crypto spot + ladders, cross-venue tapes, backfill tables

intent: Live-collected and REST-backfilled rows live in separate tables, so an analysis always knows its provenance.

elements.name: Experiment OS schema

properties.data: experiments, versions, arms, epochs, deployments, gates + results, platform revisions/snapshots, impact actions, integrity events, issues

intent: Canonical state. Markdown and chat are not authoritative once this can answer the same question.

elements.name: Alembic migrations

properties.responsibility: alembic upgrade head on every worker boot; the schema must leave a single head

intent: Schema change is part of deploy, not a manual step.

elements.name: Lifecycle: IDEA → PROBE → PAPER → LIVE_CANARY → PRODUCTION

properties.responsibility: Own experiments, Versions, epochs, arms and deployments; record every transition

intent: An experiment asks one question; a Version freezes the contract and a changed question is a new Version, never an edit.
An epoch is a changed world — evidence never pools across a non-poolable boundary.
PAUSED / RETIRED are reachable from any stage.

elements.name: Pre-registered gates + evaluator

properties.approvalCriteria: a recorded evaluator PASS on a pre-registered gate; HOLD on thin sample is correct

intent: Gates decide promotions, not P&L. Automatic evaluation is allowed; automatic promotion never is.
A gate is never re-interpreted after results are seen, and a dry run authorizes nothing.

elements.name: Enforcement (NEW_ONLY)

properties.responsibility: Refuse writes from any tag not registered to an active deployment arm

intent: Refused at the write path, not warned about. Existing books are grandfathered but may not silently evolve.

elements.name: Platform revisions + impact

properties.responsibility: Record a change to shared semantics (fees, fills, taxonomy, execution, risk, provenance, metrics) and force a disposition per affected experiment

intent: A shared-semantics change silently invalidates evidence, so it cannot activate until every affected experiment has been dispositioned.

elements.name: Issues (durable problems)

properties.responsibility: Hold anomalies, suspected defects, incidents and open scientific questions as state with an append-only event history

intent: A ticket routes work to the role that owns the problem — there is no fixer role.
It never changes a lifecycle state, gate, verdict or exposure as a side effect.

elements.name: Operator (one person)
intent: North star: $100/month realized profit — not win rate, not book count.

elements.name: Agent session (Claude)

properties.role: research / build / ops, bounded by its session role
permissions: read everything via the ops channel
write only through the audited envelope

intent: Runs in a sandbox that cannot reach Railway, Postgres or most third-party APIs.

elements.name: Session roles (sticky, bound writes)
intent: An architectural constraint, not documentation: a read-only role that finds a needed write recommends the owning role instead of quietly becoming a write session.

elements.name: Ops channel (`ops` branch → GitHub Actions)
intent: The runner checks out DEFAULT-branch code and runs it against a read-only database role, then commits the result back.
Single-slot and shared: always use a unique id and read back your own result file.

elements.name: Read-only analyses (`scripts/`)

properties.responsibility: Self-contained scorecards, probes and sweeps: weather scoring/model check/exit sweep, mm backtests, parity readouts, tape studies

intent: Stdlib-only because the ops runner cannot import the worker package.

elements.name: Production-write envelopes (single slot)
intent: The ONLY write path that does not run inside the worker's own cycle: a strictly validated envelope, consumed once at boot against a durable receipt.
Three disjoint transports on purpose — never one shared vocabulary.

elements.name: Read-only dashboards

properties.responsibility: Operator views of books, positions and live state

intent: Read-only by construction — the worker remains the only writer.

elements.name: Why the machinery exists
intent: $100/month realized profit across all strategies is the goal; research proving a book is −EV still counts as progress.
Most of this system is machinery for deciding whether an edge is real — because a paper edge that dies on contact with fills, fees or queue position is the default outcome.

connections.label: signed requests
intent: Auth failure is fatal to the cycle rather than degraded.

connections.label: markets + order books
intent: A fetch failure is recorded as a failure — never inferred as an empty universe.

connections.label: boot or exit
intent: Nothing downstream starts until config, credentials and the database all validate.

connections.label: book / variant specs
intent: Book specs are parsed and validated before a cycle runs, so a malformed book never half-trades.

connections.label: declares its universe
intent: An unknown contract is never swept into a book that did not ask for it.

connections.label: entry rule + edge
intent: Each book turns the same tape into its own candidates — that is the whole experiment.

connections.label: order intent
intent: Every intent, paper or live, passes the same gate.

connections.label: passed (all gates)
intent: The gate that stops live is recorded, not just enforced — it is evidence for the parity study.

connections.label: real orders
intent: The only edge in this diagram that spends money.

connections.label: twin armed at the same instant
intent: Fresh tags with no inherited paper state; the twin stands down whenever live does.

connections.label: live knobs, paper fills
intent: Same maker price rule, sizing, open cap and spread gate — only the fill assumption differs.

connections.label: per-candidate parity events
intent: Records incumbent paper book vs twin vs the real live outcome, including the exact gate that stopped live.

properties.behaviorWhenDown: weather books skip; other books unaffected

connections.label: cross-venue implied prices

properties.matchedOn: same station / same day / normalized team

intent: Only used where the settlement source genuinely matches — otherwise it is a different bet, not a mispricing.

connections.label: collected research datasets
intent: Collection runs ride along the trading cycle: the dataset accumulates whether or not a book trades on it yet.

connections.label: upgrade head on boot
intent: Migrations must leave a single head.

connections.label: unregistered tag refused
intent: New experimental activity must originate in Experiment OS — the refusal happens at the write path.

connections.label: arm only via service.arm_live_canary
intent: Fresh tags, a twin at the same instant, a pre-registered risk envelope — structural, because it once failed in practice.

connections.label: recorded transitions
intent: A lifecycle move is a recorded transition, never a side effect of merging code.

connections.label: recorded verdict authorizes a transition
intent: Only a recorded evaluator PASS authorizes a move; a hand-written or stale PASS never does.

connections.label: promote / pause / retire the tag that may trade
intent: Closes the loop: books generate evidence, gates read it, the lifecycle decides which books keep running.

connections.label: impact disposition before activation
intent: Every affected active experiment must be dispositioned before shared semantics change.

connections.label: routes work to the owning role
intent: There is no fixer role: a problem is routed to whoever already owns that surface.

properties.behaviorWhenDown: fleet pauses under its own budget rules

connections.label: replay only — no live path
intent: Bounded neighbourhood replay against the stored tape; it returns evidence, it does not trade.

connections.label: agent books register like any other
intent: The fleet gets no exemption from enforcement, gates or the arming ritual.

connections.label: triaged by the Evo Ticket Workshop
intent: Delivered capabilities are closed out so the queue reflects reality.

connections.label: names the session role
intent: The role is chosen once and is sticky for the session.

connections.label: push request.json
intent: The sandbox has no route to Railway or Postgres, so every production read goes through here.

connections.label: runs default-branch code
intent: A change on a feature branch cannot be exercised against production until it merges — plan measurement around that.

connections.label: SELECT-only role

properties.enforcement: server-side; no writable path may be added

intent: Read-only by design — the worker stays the only writer.

connections.label: result committed back to `ops`
intent: Poll for your own per-id result, not the shared pointer; budget minutes, and a missing file means 'not yet'.

connections.label: validated envelope (batched)
intent: Single-slot: send a whole workflow as one array, and expect a refusal while another session's envelope is unconsumed.

connections.label: executed once at worker boot
intent: Registering a Version, epoch or Platform Revision is necessarily an operator action, because only the worker holds a writable DATABASE_URL.

connections.label: explicit arming for real money
intent: Expanding exposure needs confirmation; reducing it follows kill-switch semantics.

connections.label: scorecards feed the gate read
intent: Analyses inform a verdict; they never are one — only a recorded evaluator PASS authorizes a transition.

metadata.altitude: high-level: major systems, flows and invariants only — not every module
